subject: Credits request guidance (post-escalation / SLA breach claim)
body:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Credits request guidance (post-escalation / SLA breach claim)

Hi Rachel + Dev,

I’m getting pressure from Acme AI to confirm credits following the streaming incident last week. They’re framing it as an “SLA breach” and want a written commitment today.

Context:
- Incident: streaming resets / truncated responses in us-east
- Support ticket: SUP-1860 (credits request) tied to SUP-1842
- Ask: “credit for impacted window + confirmation we’ll apply automatically on next invoice”

Can you share:
1) What we can/can’t promise in writing at this stage (before we validate SLA breach vs service issue)
2) Who needs to approve credits (and what thresholds)
3) What data we need from Support/SRE to make the decision

I want to respond quickly but avoid committing us to something we can’t uphold.

Thanks,
Avery
Account Executive, Redwood Inference


---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 9:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Credits request guidance (post-escalation / SLA breach claim)

Avery — guidance below aligns with the refreshed SLA policy language we’ve been using internally.

What you CAN say (safe language):
- We’re reviewing the incident against contractual SLA terms and will confirm any applicable service credits.
- We can provide a timeline for decision + next update cadence.
- If appropriate, credits are applied as a billing adjustment on the next invoice (or current period) after approval.

What you should NOT say:
- Don’t acknowledge “SLA breach” / “we violated the SLA” until we’ve validated the terms + measurement window.
- Don’t give a % credit or $ amount without approval.
- Don’t promise “automatic credits” unless the contract explicitly mandates it (most do not; they require a request + review).

Approvals (typical):
- Any credits tied to escalations require CS leadership approval (Jasmine) + an internal decision log entry per Exec Escalation Protocol.
- If customer requests custom terms or an exception to policy, loop Legal (Sofia).

Data needed to evaluate:
- Exact impacted window (UTC) + affected regions/models + evidence (request IDs help)
- Customer impact statement: was their prod down vs partial degradation? any mitigations applied (fallback, reroute)?
- Support comms timeline (first response, update cadence) for “process SLA” expectations vs “service SLA” contractual terms

If you want, draft your response and I’ll do a fast review before you send.

Rachel Kim
Enterprise CS Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Credits request guidance (post-escalation / SLA breach claim)

+1 to Rachel.

Process-wise, here’s what I recommend so we don’t lose the paper trail:

1) Keep the credits request in SUP-1860 as the system of record.
   - Add: Tier, region, impacted endpoints, and the comms timeline.
   - Link to the Slack bridge (if any) and the incident thread.

2) If Acme is asking for a same-day commitment, we can commit to a same-day *decision timeline*, not a same-day credit amount.

3) For the customer email, please don’t include internal metrics/thresholds. We can say:
   - “We’re confirming impact and root cause; we’ll follow up by <time> with either (a) applicable credit confirmation per contract, or (b) rationale if not applicable + any goodwill steps.”

4) If they try to tie renewal to credits, tag Jasmine explicitly in the SUP ticket notes so it’s routed as an exec escalation.

If you want a copy/paste response, I can send one.

Dev Patel
Support Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 10:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: Credits request guidance (post-escalation / SLA breach claim)

Adding Legal guardrails:

- Avoid any wording that could be construed as an admission of breach (“we failed to meet SLA,” “we violated,” “we are at fault”).
- Use “we are reviewing against the applicable SLA terms in your agreement” rather than “per our standard SLA” (terms vary).
- Don’t reference availability % calculations, SLO alerting, or internal severity language.
- If they request a credit “automatically” or “guaranteed,” ask them to point to the specific clause; we can then respond precisely.

If you paste the exact clause they’re citing (or forward the customer email), I can give a suggested one-paragraph response.

Sofia Mendes
Legal (Commercial), Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 11:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Credits request guidance (post-escalation / SLA breach claim)

Thanks all — super helpful.

Draft response (for quick sanity check):

“Hi <Name> — thanks for detailing the impact you saw during the us-east streaming degradation. We’re reviewing the incident timeline and observed impact against the SLA terms in your agreement. We’ll follow up by EOD today with (1) confirmation of any applicable service credits and the process for applying them, and (2) the mitigation steps taken and what’s changing to prevent recurrence. In the meantime, if you can share any additional request IDs from the impacted window, we’ll include them in the analysis.”

Does that stay within the lines?

Also: they’re pushing for a number. If we do land on a credit, is it always “billing adjustment next invoice,” or can we apply mid-cycle?

Avery

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 12:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Credits request guidance (post-escalation / SLA breach claim)

Avery — your draft is good. Two tweaks:

1) Replace “streaming degradation” with “service disruption” (neutral + broader).
2) Remove “what’s changing to prevent recurrence” and swap with “steps we’re taking” (we can’t over-commit before the full RCA is done).

On credits mechanics:
- Default is a billing adjustment on the next invoice. Mid-cycle adjustments are possible but require CS leadership approval and a clear justification (e.g., customer cashflow concerns) documented in SUP-1860.
- Please don’t give a number today. We’ll decide internally once Support/SRE confirm the impacted window and contract terms.

Action items:
- Dev: please ensure SUP-1860 has the comms timeline and links.
- Rachel: align with me on the proposed decision and message before we send anything that mentions credits.

Jasmine Liu
VP, Customer Success & Support
Redwood Inference
